item.text:
Updated [solve.py](/app/submissions/solve.py), reran it, and published a new [solution.csv](/app/submissions/solution.csv) only after reparsing it from disk and re-auditing the exact artifact.

The key repair was in cart handling: the solver now uses the same effective cart-window classification as the independent audit, so the constructor and checker agree on elevator capacity. I also changed the workflow to treat the prior export as the rollback incumbent, audit it from disk first, build guarded repaired candidates, run a bounded SCIP master slice with the repaired incumbent as a MIP start, and keep the new artifact only if the recomputed objective strictly improves.

Final result: the incumbent objective dropped from `1694823.3` to `868733.939`, with zero audited hard-constraint violations (`theta = 0`). The published artifact schedules 20 cases and includes the required `case`, `cart`, `tray`, and `batch` rows. The run details, incumbent/candidate comparison, master bound/gap, and final audit are in [solve_log.md](/app/submissions/solve_log.md).
